Institution All Family Group All Clear Select how often (in days) to receive an alert: Create Alert × Select how often (in days) to receive an alert: Apply now » Assistant Director / Senior Manager / Manager (Architecture & Project Management) Institution: Tan Tock Seng Hospital Family Group: Administration The HealthCity Novena (HCN) Master Plan was developed by Tan Tock Seng Hospital (TTSH), the flagship tertiary hospital of NHG Health, to transform the 17-hectare campus into Singapore's premier integrated hub for healthcare, education, and research - anchored in the vision of advancing patient-centric care for the 1.5 million residents of Central and North Singapore. Following the successful delivery of Phase 1, Phase 2 was launched on 9 September 2025 and marks the critical intensification of the campus. Phase 2 is anchored by two flagship developments: the new TTSH Medical Tower and the operationalization of the TTSH Pavilion. The hallmark of Phase 2, the TTSH Medical Tower will add approximately 600 acute beds, significantly strengthening TTSH's healthcare capacity for high-intensity, specialist care. It will house an expanded Emergency Department, additional operating theatres, and procedural suites, and specialist outpatient clinics, all purpose-designed to advance frailty-ready and technology-enabled care. In addition, to sustain full operational continuity throughout construction, the former Pavilion wards on campus have been transformed and reactivated as the TTSH Pavilion - a modernized facility comprising specialist clinics, laboratories, and offices. THE ROLE You will serve as the lead project manager / coordinator for the architectural and built environment components of the TTSH Medical Tower project. Beyond ensuring that construction faithfully reflects approved designs and User Group Meeting (UGM) outcomes, you will have the opportunity to shape the Healing Environment portfolio - the integrated set of disciplines that shapes how patients, visitors, and staff physically experience the completed campus. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES A. Architectural Coordination & Site Management You will ensure approved designs are executed with precision - bridging clinical requirements, consultant deliverables, and construction reality across every phase of the build. Design Coordination: Review architectural blueprints and shop drawings to verify that they accurately reflect the approved UGM requirements and Schedule of Accommodation (SOA), identifying discrepancies early and managing resolution with consultants before they reach site. Site Management: Lead regular site inspections and attend progress meetings to verify that works are being executed in accordance with technical drawings, quality standards, and the approved programme. User Liaison: Facilitate structured design review sessions with clinical and operational users, translating their requirements into actionable briefs for consultants and contractors. Documentation: Maintain accurate and complete records of milestone sign-offs, meeting minutes, design submissions, and progress payment approvals. Change Management: Manage design change requests from contractors and consultants across all architectural workstreams, assessing impact on scope, programme, and user requirements before escalating for approval. Space Planning: Develop test fit drawings and space planning layouts for clinical and non-clinical tenants across the campus, supporting decisions on department placement, space allocation, and relocation as the Medical Tower programme evolves. Minor Works: Manage the calling of tenders and oversee smaller construction and fitting-out works arising within the main TTSH campus as a result of operational linkages to the Medical Tower or Pavilion, including scope definition, contractor coordination, and works completion. B. Healing Environment Design You will manage the development and implementation of the Healing Environment framework across three interconnected disciplines, with the patient and visitor journey as the organising principle throughout. Wayfinding: Work with appointed consultants in the implementation of the campus-wide wayfinding strategy from the HealthCity Novena master plan stage, including but not limited to designs for the full patient and visitor journey, spatial configuration, colour zoning, flooring transitions, lighting, sightlines, and landmark features. Master Interior Design: Oversee, on behalf of TTSH, the master interior design brief and its execution across all patient-facing, clinical, and public spaces, ensuring design intent - materiality, colour palette, lighting strategy, furniture selection - is consistently applied across zones, and that design integrity is protected through to practical completion. Landscape Design: Manage the landscape design scope for all external and biophilic elements of the campus, ensuring landscape elements serve as active wayfinding anchors and contribute to the healing environment strategy as a coherent whole. C. Commissioning & Operational Readiness You will manage the transition from construction completion to a fully operational facility, ensuring every element is activated, tested, and ready before Day 1. Develop and maintain a master readiness timeline for the Medical Tower's architectural and environmental design workstreams, tracking activation milestones for wayfinding, interior fit-out, and landscape completion against the overall opening programme. Coordinate user familiarisation walkthroughs and pre-opening inspections, ensuring that clinical and operational teams have adequate exposure to the new spaces and that feedback is captured, assessed, and acted upon before opening. Lead the snagging and defects-rectification process for all architectural, interior, and environmental design elements, working with contractors and consultants to ensure full resolution within the defects liability period. Oversee the activation and commissioning of wayfinding systems - including physical signage, digital directories, and floor-level orientation cues - ensuring the full system is tested, operational, and legible to a first-time visitor before Day 1. Work closely with Operations, Facilities, and clinical leads to consolidate ramp-up requirements, staffing readiness for new spaces, and any outstanding design or fit-out dependencies that could affect service launch. Track readiness indicators across all environmental design workstreams, surface risks and gaps proactively, and provide timely updates to the project lead and governance committees. REQUIREMENTS Degree in Architecture, Interior Design, Building Science, or a related built environment discipline. At least 8 years (Manager), 10-12 years (Senior Manager), or 13-15 years (AD) of project management experience, with demonstrated involvement in design-to-construction transitions on major public buildings or healthcare facilities. Prior experience managing or coordinating wayfinding, master interior design, or landscape design workstreams within a large infrastructure project is strongly preferred. A clear understanding of how patients and visitors navigate large, complex buildings - and how architectural and design decisions either support or undermine that experience. Proficiency in interpreting complex architectural and technical drawings across multi-disciplinary site contexts. Working knowledge of Revit and AutoCAD; ability to read and interpret BIM models and produce or review test fit drawings and space planning layouts independently or in collaboration with consultants. Working knowledge of contract administration under PSSCOC or SIA conditions of contract, including variation orders, progress claims, and final accounts. Experience in FFE procurement and installation coordination within a healthcare or major institutional building project is an advantage. Strong stakeholder coordination skills, with the ability to manage clinical users, specialist consultants, and main contractors concurrently. Meticulous attention to design consistency, documentation accuracy, and milestone accountability. It serves as the organising platform for multiple virtual and distributed care models, enabling patients to access the right care, at the right time, in the right place. Since its inception in 2020, NUHS@Home has rapidly grown into a critical pillar of NUHS’ vision for healthcare that is integrated, agile, and closer to the patient. More than a single service, it represents a new architecture for care delivery – one where geography no longer dictates access, and recovery happens where patients feel safest, supported, and most at home. The Role We are seeking an experienced, strategic and forward-thinking Senior Manager / Assistant Director, Human Resource . Reporting to the Head of Human Resource, you will serve as a trusted HR leader and strategic business partner to the NUHS@Home leadership team and key stakeholders. This is a hands-on leadership role for someone who enjoys driving people strategies that support workforce transformation, talent development, employee engagement and organisational growth, while leading the HR team and providing tactical advice and practical solutions across the employee lifecycle. As a key member of the NUHS@Home leadership team, you will play an important role in shaping the people agenda and enabling the continued growth and evolution of the NUHS@Home care delivery model. You will also contribute to leadership continuity for the HR function by supporting the Head of Human Resource on designated matters and strengthening succession coverage within the HR team. What you will own Strategic HR Business Partnering Build strong, trusted relationships with business leaders and stakeholders, providing strategic advice and practical HR solutions that support organisational priorities and business outcomes. Advise leaders on the interpretation and application of HR policies and procedures, employment legislation, performance management, manpower planning, resourcing, rewards and other people-related matters. Partner with Talent Acquisition to develop and implement targeted recruitment strategies aligned with NUHS@Home manpower plans, workforce requirements and growth priorities, including the review and approval of compensation recommendations. Lead the annual manpower planning and budgeting exercise, ensuring alignment with organisational priorities, workforce requirements and financial objectives. Support organisational transformation, change management and workforce redesign initiatives to enable the growth and evolution of NUHS@Home’s care delivery model. Analyse workforce trends, employee engagement data, attrition metrics and other manpower indicators to generate insights and recommendations for organisational and workforce planning, and the effective management of organisational risks. Oversee employee lifecycle matters through the HR team, including employee enquiries, employment changes, transfers, appointments and exit processes, in accordance with HR policies and procedures. People Leadership and Development Lead, manage and develop the HR team to ensure the effective, professional and timely delivery of HR plans, programmes, processes and services. Provide direction, coaching and support to build HR capability, strengthen service delivery and promote a high-performing team culture. Foster close collaboration with relevant Group HR Centres of Excellence to deliver integrated and value-adding people solutions. Employee Engagement, Talent and Workforce Development Drive employee engagement initiatives that strengthen workplace culture, employee experience, productivity and retention. Work with leaders to identify organisational capability gaps and support organisation design, workforce planning, capability-building and talent pipeline initiatives. Promote a culture of continuous learning, collaboration, accountability and service excellence. Governance, Policy and Stakeholder Collaboration Collaborate with NUHS Group HR Centres of Excellence and relevant stakeholders to implement HR projects, programmes and initiatives. Work with the Centres of Excellence to review and enhance HR policies, guidelines and processes to ensure their relevance to NUHS@Home and compliance with applicable regulatory requirements. Contribute to NUHS, Ministry of Manpower (MOM), Ministry of Health (MOH), MOH Holdings (MOHH), NUHS@Home and Human Resource projects, events, governance initiatives, policy reviews and committees, as assigned or appointed. Who You Are This role is suited to an experienced HR leader who is able to operate at both strategic and operational levels: shaping the people agenda, advising senior stakeholders, leading a small HR team, and translating organisational priorities into practical workforce and talent solutions. Background A bachelor’s degree in Human Resource Management, Business Management or a related discipline. At least 10 years of relevant HR experience, preferably within the healthcare sector, with a strong track record in HR business partnering, organisational transformation, workforce redesign and people management. Demonstrated ability to influence and partner with business leaders to achieve strategic business and people outcomes. Demonstrated experience leading, coaching and developing HR professionals or business partners. Strong knowledge of HR practices, including employee relations, performance management, manpower planning, talent management, resourcing and rewards. Proven leadership and collaboration skills, with the ability to develop team members, build effective partnerships across functions and work independently with a high degree of initiative. Strong analytical, problem-solving and decision-making skills, with the ability to translate workforce data and insights into actionable recommendations. Proficient in Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel and PowerPoint, with experience in workforce analytics, manpower reporting, budgeting and presentation development. Experience in healthcare operations, change management or organisational capability-building would be an advantage. What we offer An opportunity to help shape NUHS’ healthcare workforce of the future and the future of healthcare delivery in Singapore. Meaningful ownership and decision-making responsibility in a high-growth healthcare transformation programme. The opportunity to contribute to the development of NUHS@Home and its future leadership capability as the programme scales. Why Join Us NUHS@Home is redefining care delivery by creating Singapore’s virtual campus for comprehensive clinical care through a digital-first approach. You will contribute to workforce transformation and the future of healthcare delivery in Singapore and beyond. Influence Strategic Decisions Partner with senior leadership, clinicians, project consultants, and government agencies to drive critical commercial and procurement decisions. Overview We are seeking an experienced and highly motivated Cost & Contracts Leader to head the Cost & Contracts Section within the NUH Development Office. In this strategic leadership role, you will oversee the commercial, cost management, procurement, and contract administration functions for one of Singapore's most significant healthcare redevelopment programmes. You will play a critical role in ensuring that project investments are optimised, procurement strategies are effective, and contracts are managed proactively to support the successful delivery of NUH's future healthcare infrastructure. Working closely with consultants, contractors, development agents, and internal stakeholders, you will provide commercial leadership across the entire project lifecycle, from planning and design through construction, commissioning, and project close-out. Strategic Cost Planning & Commercial Leadership Lead the development and management of project budgets, cost plans, estimates, and financial forecasts for infrastructure works and Furniture, Fixtures & Equipment (FF&E). Provide strategic advice on project affordability, value optimisation, and cost management throughout the project lifecycle. Establish and maintain robust cost control frameworks to ensure alignment with approved budgets and project objectives. Oversee cashflow forecasting, expenditure tracking, and financial reporting to support effective decision-making. Ensure the utilisation of project funds, procurement activities, and contract administration comply with applicable organisational policies, governance requirements, and regulatory frameworks. Procurement & Contract Management Lead the planning and execution of procurement activities in collaboration with development agents, consultants, and project stakeholders. Develop procurement strategies, contract packaging approaches, and tendering plans that achieve value for money while ensuring appropriate risk allocation. Review and oversee the preparation of tender estimates, procurement documents, evaluation processes, and award recommendations. Provide leadership in contract administration, including management of variations, claims, disputes, risk mitigation measures, and contractual compliance. Ensure contracts are administered effectively to safeguard NUH's commercial and operational interests. Stakeholder Engagement & Project Delivery Partner closely with users, consultants, contractors, and project teams to provide commercial guidance and facilitate timely decision-making. Support project planning and delivery by ensuring cost and contractual considerations are incorporated into key project decisions. Lead discussions and negotiations on commercial matters while maintaining productive stakeholder relationships. Drive alignment across multiple stakeholders to support project timelines, budget objectives, and delivery outcomes. Governance, Risk & Process Excellence Ensure all procurement, cost management, and contract administration activities are conducted in accordance with NUHS and cluster governance requirements. Establish robust documentation, reporting, and audit-ready records to support project accountability and transparency. Identify, assess, and manage commercial and contractual risks throughout the project lifecycle. Promote continuous improvement through the enhancement of systems, processes, and best practices. Leadership & Strategic Development Lead, mentor, and develop a high-performing Cost & Contracts team. Foster a culture of collaboration, accountability, and professional excellence. Keep abreast of industry developments, healthcare infrastructure trends, procurement innovations, and emerging commercial practices. Undertake other responsibilities and strategic initiatives supporting hospital redevelopment and infrastructure development. Requirements Bachelor's Degree in Quantity Surveying, Construction Management, Architecture, Civil & Structural Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related built environment discipline. At least 15 years of relevant experience in quantity surveying, cost management, commercial management, procurement, and/or contract administration. Demonstrated experience managing major infrastructure, healthcare, institutional, or public sector development projects. Healthcare infrastructure project experience will be highly advantageous. Strong understanding of procurement strategies, contract forms, commercial risk management, and cost control principles. Excellent analytical, negotiation, and problem-solving capabilities. Strong interpersonal and communication skills with the ability to influence and build consensus across diverse stakeholder groups. Highly organised, resourceful, and capable of managing multiple priorities within a complex and fast-paced environment. Strong written communication and presentation skills. Under the MOH Medical Service Scheme employment, you will bring your clinical lens and expertise to national healthcare policies and influence decisions that shape the health of Singapore. jobs.title: Manager/Assistant Director (Case Management), Community Relations Unit
jobs.jd: Posting Date: 14 Sep 2026. Closing on 30 Sep 2026. The Community Relations Unit (CRU) was set up to address severe neighbour noise disputes and hoarding cases. CRU was piloted in Tampines HDB estates from April 2025, and the model was expanded nationwide on 1 September 2026. It is part of the enhancements to the Community Disputes Management Framework. While most neighbour disputes can and should be resolved through dialogue and mediation, a small number involve excessive and prolonged noise disturbances that cause significant distress to multiple residents. CRU focuses on these severe neighbour noise cases across public and private housing estates. CRU also works closely with HDB and PA on the enforcement of Mediation Directions, which require neighbours to attend mediation at the Community Mediation Centre. jobs.title: [PMO-NSCS] Assistant Director (Policy 3)
jobs.jd: Posting Date: 11 Sep 2026. Closing on 25 Sep 2026. The National Security Coordination Secretariat (NSCS) is a unit under the Prime Minister's Office responsible for national security planning and coordination. NSCS works with agencies and stakeholders to develop and co-ordinate strategies to address national security concerns. NSCS also works with agencies to anticipate and identify emergent security risks, and to build up capabilities and resources to deal with these. The role will give you the opportunity to strengthen: • Critical Thinking: You will lead your team to keep abreast of national security developments and synthesise information across domains (geopolitical, economic, social, environment, information, etc.) to identify and analyse cross-cutting national security risks. These include economic security risks, digital security risks, concentration risks, and inter-dependency risks. • Systems Thinking: You will lead your team to integrate analysis of external developments with assessments of Singapore’s vulnerabilities and how the latter will change over time. You will recommend the best way to structure the Whole-of-Government response to the risk. This will require you to suggest constructive solutions which balance multiple policy considerations across domains. For specific risks, you could contribute to the full policy value-chain from strategic planning, policy formulation, policy-operations, to comms and implementation (e.g., legislation). • Influence: You will need to mobilise colleagues from a wide range of agencies, with different mandates and policy considerations, to work with you on the overall risk assessment. You will need to build consensus on the risk level Singapore can live with and the Whole-of-Government action needed to mitigate the risks. This would require you to build extensive and deep networks across domains and seniority levels, and develop a deep understanding of their considerations and constraints. You will work in a team: • To hunt out Singapore’s cross-cutting vulnerabilities (e.g., in critical infrastructure, social resilience) that could be exploited/ disrupted and build shared risk pictures (through data analysis and/ or policy analysis) to inform decision-making by public sector leaders. • To mobilise collective Whole-of-Government efforts to tackle complex, collective-action problems. This could involve putting forth recommendations which could sub-optimise agency-specific objectives to achieve better national outcomes. Depending on your performance and experience, you could be given the opportunity to lead a team or project. • At least five years of policy experience preferred; • Intellectual curiosity, and clear logical and systems thinking; • Excellent writing skills to deliver analyses synthesising information from multiple domains, including data-driven outputs; • Experience engaging multiple agencies and stakeholders, with skills to listen empathetically, sense dynamics, and persuade and negotiate across agencies and seniority levels to achieve desired outcomes; • Ability to move between macro and micro perspectives; • Preferably an intuitive grasp of Singapore’s security imperatives; • Interest in current affairs; • Ability to work in a dynamic environment and pick up new skills/ domain knowledge if necessary; and • Proactive, articulate, purpose-driven, persistent . We may refer you as a potential candidate for vacancies in other agencies we assessed you to be suitable for. By applying for this job, you are aware of, and are also giving NSCS consent for the cross referral. If you do not wish to be cross referred, please inform us via this link: https://go.gov.sg/candidateoptout.

The Family Life Group (FLG)’s goal is to build strong marriages and resilient families, helping them navigate key life transitions. The challenges facing families are becoming more complex. Singapore also faces persistent low fertility rate. Addressing these challenges will require us to understand families, connect insights across systems so as to design better intervention and continuously improve how the Government serves Singaporeans. As the central coordination division for FLG, the Operations Planning & Transformation (OPT) Division drives ops strategy, corporate planning, transformation, data and digitalisation, capability development and engagement strategies for FLG. The Division works closely with FLG divisions, other MSF groups and Whole-of-Government partners to translate strategic priorities into effective implementation and sustainable organisational capabilities. Data and analytics are increasingly important to how Government understands the needs of families, formulates policy, allocates resources and delivers services. As the volume and complexity of data grows, FLG needs strong data foundations, trusted and timely information, and the ability to translate data into insights and decisions. AI is also increasingly becoming part of data platform and analytics stack. As Deputy Director/Senior Deputy Director (Family Data, Analytics and AI), you will lead FLG's efforts to strengthen its data foundations, leverage AI and turn family data into actionable insights that improve policy, programmes, operations and service delivery. You will oversee the Family Data Hub as FLG's strategic data product, strengthen data governance and analytics capabilities, and enable the responsible adoption of AI and emerging technologies. Reporting to the Director, OPT, you will work closely with senior management, policy and service divisions across FLG, MSF's data and digital teams, Whole-of-Government partners and technology providers. You will play an instrumental role in shaping the strategic direction, priorities and roadmap for family data, analytics and AI for FLG, while ensuring that initiatives are translated into impact for families. The role combines strategic leadership, product management, data governance, analytics, stakeholder engagement and transformation. The successful candidate will be expected to connect these disciplines and build the organisational capability needed for FLG to become increasingly data-driven and AI-enabled. Key Responsibilities 1) Lead FLG’s data, analytics and AI strategy • Develop and lead strategy to strengthen data foundation and use of AI across FLG, aligned with MSF and whole-of-Government priorities; • Identify and prioritise opportunities to use data, analytics and AI to enable faster and better-informed decisions, improve service delivery and enhance operational effectiveness; • Build partnerships across FLG and relevant stakeholders to drive adoption and realise the value of data. 2) Own and drive Family Data Hub as the strategic data product for Family Life Group • Serve as the business owner and product lead for the Family Data Hub, including the Family Status Repository (FSR) as the single source of truth for marital and family information; • Set the product vision, objectives and key results as well as the product roadmap for the Family Data Hub, balancing user needs, data quality, timeliness, data governance, technology considerations and implementation capacity; • Drive adoption and use of the Family Data Hub across FLG, ensuring that the product delivers value to users in FLG and whole-of-government; • Drive continuous improvement of Family Data Hub to ensure that it remains relevant, trusted and fit for emerging policy and service needs; • Work with technical and business stakeholders to translate strategic requirements into viable

jobs.title: Deputy Director (International Brand Office), Comms & Engagement Div
jobs.jd: Posting Date: 7 Sep 2026. Closing on 30 Sep 2026. MTI’s Communications and Engagement Division (CED), is hiring a Deputy Director for its International Brand Office (IBO). Established in 2025, IBO is responsible for building awareness of Singapore with an international business audience and providing guidance to other government agencies on their international branding and marketing. The Deputy Director heads up the IBO and reports to Director (CED). (a) Leadership and management • Set IBO’s overall direction, strategy and budget • Lead a team of three officers to achieve IBO’s objectives • Update MTI senior management on IBO’s strategy and work (b) International brand strategy • Oversee and periodically revisit a Singapore brand narrative for international audiences, which includes brand truths, brand purpose, and a creative brand platform • Align and socialize the brand narrative with other government agencies with a stake in the Singapore brand internationally – this includes MTI’s statutory boards as well as other Ministries such as the Ministry of Digital Development and Information (MDDI) • If necessary, commission brand health studies and/or other relevant research to analyse international perceptions of the Singapore brand (c) Brand execution and campaigns • Increase awareness and positive perceptions of Singapore through a series of campaigns and marketing & comms activities, drawing on the refreshed brand narrative in (b). This includes determining what types of campaigns and activities are needed given the current state of the Singapore brand; examples include brand films, paid media, brand partnerships, event activations, earned media outreach, and public comms • Work with MTI-CED and other government organizations on amplifying IBO’s campaigns through their channels (d) Brand governance and coordination • Drive consistent application of the Singapore brand in other government agencies’ international campaigns. This includes compelling other agencies to adopt a brand guide developed by IBO • Coordinate and streamline the spectrum of international brand sensemaking efforts – such as brand health studies – being conducted across the MTI family, MDDI, and other government organizations • Coordinate and monitor efforts by other organizations to amplify the Singapore brand to an international audience (e) Others • Drive or support other relevant MTI work as needed, including within and outside of MTI-CED • At least 12 years’ working experience, preferably in B2B marketing or the public sector. jobs.title: Deputy/Assistant Director, AML Policy (1-Year Contract)
jobs.jd: Posting Date: 3 Sep 2026. Closing on 29 Sep 2026. jobs.jd: Posting Date: 15 Sep 2026. Closing on 29 Sep 2026. At MSE and our family of agencies – PUB, NEA, and SFA – we drive sustainability and resilience initiatives that improve the everyday lives of Singaporeans. As part of the MSE Family, you will be at the forefront of innovation, leading efforts to safeguard water resources, protect public health, and ensure food safety. Through partnerships across sectors, we tackle evolving challenges while fostering an inclusive, safe, and supportive workplace. Join us in shaping Singapore’s sustainable future and making a lasting impact on the everyday lives of generations to come. The Water and Food Policy Division (WFPD) works closely with the Public Utilities Board (PUB) and the Singapore Food Agency (SFA) to formulate, review, and implement a broad range of policies and strategies to ensure the supply of water and safe food for Singapore. Singapore imports more than 90% of our food from over 180 countries and regions. This makes us vulnerable to global food supply disruptions, arising from factors including disease outbreaks, geopolitical tensions and climate change. Our approach to food resilience entails four pillars – import diversification, global partnerships, stockpile and grow local – working together to ensure Singaporeans always have food on our tables, even when faced with threats. As food resilience challenges heighten both globally and locally, it is key to regularly review our strategies to ensure our regime remains robust. Apart from securing our food supply, we have to ensure that the food is safe to eat. Food safety covers a broad range of issues from fark-to-fork, from produce grown in farms to food that is served at your favourite hawker centre and coffeeshop. With new food innovations such as alternative proteins and an evolving food ecosystem increasingly dependent on new technologies, we have to look ahead of the curve to ensure that our policies, strategies and regulations are ready to deal with such complexities, including new emerging risks and industry developments. You will work with a dynamic, fast-paced team, working closely with agencies such as SFA, to review, develop and implement policies and programmes that contribute to the strategic objectives of securing a supply of safe food for Singapore. You will also be involved in policies and joint programmes that intersect with other policy areas within the MSE family, thus contributing to wider sustainability and public health issues. - Work with SFA and other partner agencies to formulate and review strategies, policies and legislation/regulations to strengthen Singapore’s food safety and food resilience regime - Work with communications teams to sharpen public communications plans and messages relating to food safety and food resilience issues - Engage a variety of stakeholders - such as associations/industry players, academics and the public - to push the frontiers of food safety and food resilience - Monitor and analyse global food supply and demand trends, and shape policies to mitigate the risks and vulnerabilities in Singapore’s food supplies - Tertiary Qualifications - Strong analytical and systems thinking skills - Excellent writing, communication, and presentation skills - Team player with strong inter-personal skills - Ability to apply systems thinking - Able to work independently and be resourceful in problem solving

The energy crisis after COVID and the war in Ukraine have upended the global energy ecosystem. The climate crisis compels all countries to accelerate their pace of decarbonisation, even as they struggle with energy costs and unpredictable supply chain shocks. Amidst this backdrop, Singapore needs a stable, reliable, and cost competitive energy system that keeps the lights on and safeguards our economic competitiveness and dynamism.
